title: The Rearview
hook: My dad's one rule for the drive home: after the tunnel, never look in the rearview mirror.
lines: Every Thanksgiving, Dad drove us home through the mountains. And every year, the same warning.
After the tunnel, never look in the rearview mirror. And if you do... don't let her see you look.
He never said who she was.
This year, Dad was too tired, so I drove. He was asleep before we reached the tunnel.
When we came out the other side, I checked the mirror. Just habit.
There was a woman in the back seat.
Gray coat. Soaking wet. Long black hair hanging over her face... staring down at the floor.
I snapped my eyes back to the road. I drove twenty miles without breathing.
Behind me, I could hear water... dripping onto the seat.
At the first gas station, I shook Dad awake and told him everything.
He went pale. Did she see you look?
No, I said. She never looked up.
Dad closed his eyes... and let out a long, slow breath.
Then I glanced at the mirror one last time.
Her head was up now. And through all that wet hair... she was smiling at me.
